President Abelardo de la Espriella says police and military have been deployed as situation unfolds in Cartagena.
About 25 people are being held hostage at a supermarket in the Colombian city of Cartagena, where a group of armed men fled after an unsuccessful attempt to rob an armoured vehicle.
President Abelardo de la Espriella said on Tuesday that police and armed forces have been deployed to the scene.
He explained that the robbers sought refuge in a nearby store after security camera operators alerted police to the attempted robbery.
“Thirty people were kidnapped, five of whom have already been released. They are older women,” said de la Espriella. “All the capabilities of our various security forces have now been deployed, including special units.”
Images from the Reuters news agency showed heavily armed police and military personnel outside the Exito supermarket in the neighbourhood of La Castellana.
Unverified footage shared on social media appeared to show people inside the market kneeling against the windows with their hands bound.
The incident comes as de la Espriella, who campaigned on a promise to crack down on crime, faces a series of high-profile incidents that underscore the country’s ongoing issues with violence and insecurity.
The president made his remarks from the city of Villavicencio, where he had travelled in the aftermath of a recent car bombing the government has attributed to an armed group.
Already, politicians like former left-wing President Gustavo Petro have weighed in on the incident, blaming failures in de la Espriella’s security platform.
“The root cause of this violence is the impoverishment of the population, brought about by the collapse of the tourism sector,” Petro, de la Espriella’s predecessor, wrote on social media.
“Destroying tourism — through state-sanctioned violence, such as the desecration of corpses, and by making death the central theme of presidential discourse — has dismantled a dynamic source of wealth that once attracted 7 million foreign tourists.”
De la Espriella beat Petro’s handpicked successor, Senator Ivan Cepeda, in a June 21 run-off election.

President says 15 people released and Cartagena incident stems from botched robbery by ‘common criminals’
Armed and masked men have been holding people hostage in a supermarket since early Tuesday morning in Cartagena, one of Colombia’s most popular tourist cities.
The country’s president, Abelardo de la Espriella, said 30 people had initially been taken hostage, but five had been released, and hours later local media reported that another 10 had also been freed.
The far-right president added that, despite the context of growing violence perpetrated by criminal groups involved in the country’s decades-long armed conflict, the hostage-taking appeared to have stemmed from a botched robbery carried out by “common criminals”.
The past few days have been particularly challenging in the South American country, with a car bomb and a drone attack killing one person and leaving nearly 30 injured.
The supermarket where the hostages are being held is just six miles from the old city and its 500-year-old fortress walls overlooking the Caribbean. Hundreds of thousands of visitors are drawn to Cartagena every year.
The gunmen reportedly arrived at about 8.30am local time at an Éxito supermarket in La Castellana neighbourhood and, according to Colombia’s president, the group planned to rob an armoured cash-in-transit vehicle that was due to collect the previous day’s takings from the store.
After spotting the movement on security cameras, employees reportedly alerted the national police, who surrounded the supermarket.
“My son is there,” Jacob Perez, the father of one of the workers reportedly held hostage, told Agence France-Presse. “He didn’t leave work and he’s not answering his phone. I think they took it from him,” he said.
Customers were also believed to be among the hostages. The five people initially released were “older women”, according to De la Espriella. Caracol Radio later reported that another 10 had been freed.
Footage shared on social media showed dozens of people rushing out of the supermarket, while local media outlets showed snipers positioned on nearby buildings in what appeared to be a standoff between the armed men and police.
De la Espriella, known for his populist rhetoric and an “iron fist” approach to crime – he sometimes wears a gun on his waist and has posed beside the bodies of people killed by police – has been in office for just over three months, and said the hours-long standoff at the supermarket “will turn out well for the hostages, but I’m not so sure it will turn out quite so well for the hostage-takers”.
He addressed the case at a press conference in Villavicencio, about 684 miles inland, where he was dealing with the aftermath of an attack on Monday night in which a car bomb was detonated outside the headquarters of the Meta departmental government.
More than 20 people were injured and a security guard was killed, and the president attributed the attack to a dissident faction of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc).
“Narco-terrorism is desperate because we are confronting it decisively. It intends to intimidate us and force us to retreat in search of another false peace process,” the president said, referring to the landmark 2016 peace deal between the government and the Farc – whose signing marked its 10th anniversary on Tuesday.
Internationally recognised for substantially reducing violence, the deal alone could not bring the decades-long armed conflict to a definitive end. Subsequent administrations were slow to implement the agreement, which was rejected by Farc dissidents and other rebel factions.
In the early hours of Monday, in another part of the country, gunmen believed to belong to the ELN, an armed group that never signed a peace deal, used drones to drop bombs on the local police command in the city of Cúcuta. Instead they hit homes and injured three civilians, including an 18-month-old baby.
Although drone attacks by criminal groups have become increasingly common, it was the first time they had targeted a departmental capital.

Arsenal’s sky-high standards are slipping. For the second time in four days, Mikel Arteta’s side found themselves a goal up at half-time and apparently coasting toward victory, only for their opponents to rouse themselves and earn a deserved draw. After Newcastle on Saturday , this time it was an impressive Borussia Dortmund who became only the second side to take points off Arsenal in their past 15 group stage games in this competition. It could have been worse had an offside flag not ruled out Jobe ­Bellingham’s goal after Max Beier equalised a thunderbolt from Viktor Gyökeres.
But the much-maligned Sweden striker was guilty of a glaring miss late on as Arsenal laid siege to Dortmund’s goal, racking up 30 shots by the final whistle. The German side had to hang on for a result that gave their travelling fans a night to remember, although Arteta admitted his players must be more clinical when Real Madrid and Jude Bellingham visit north London in a fortnight.
“We want to win every game and today we didn’t manage to make that difference in the scoring unfortunately,” he said. “There is an element of luck, there is an element of us finishing the actions better. It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn’t ended up in the back of the net.”
While neither Max Dowman nor Ethan Nwaneri – the latter on loan at Dortmund from the Gunners – made it off the bench, the exploits of another teenager were on the Arsenal supporters’ lips on their way to the ground. A stunning solo goal from 14-year-old Luis Muñoz – an England Under-15 international who is the youngest player ever to feature in the Uefa Youth League – against Dortmund earlier in the day showed that Arsenal’s conveyor belt of talent continues to produce. Aside from Myles Lewis-Skelly – a relative veteran these days at 20 – Arteta opted for experience as he made six changes, including Kepa Arrizabalaga deputising in goal for the injured David Raya.
Dortmund have not been crowned German champions since Jürgen Klopp’s days in 2012 but lead the Bundesliga by two points from Bayern Munich. Like Arsenal, Niko Kovac’s side have relied on a solid defence and they showed real resilience in the second half after drawing level. They look a decent bet for a top-eight finish on this showing.
Arrizabalaga had started only once this season, in the Carabao Cup win over Ipswich , and the former Spain goalkeeper was largely a spectator again for the first half as Arsenal assumed total control. Christos Tzolis had two early sighters after being set up by the rejuvenated Noni Madueke but the Dortmund goalkeeper, Gregor Kobel, still seemed surprised by the power with which Gyökeres struck the ball in the 10th minute when he was fed by the England forward.
He was only introduced in the fourth minute of stoppage time against Newcastle as Arsenal chased a winner at the weekend but clearly had a point to prove as his shot arrowed into the back of the net from outside the area.
If only Gyökeres could have been so clinical when easier chances came his way and the 28-year-old’s long-term future remains in doubt given Arteta’s preference for Kai Havertz. “I think he had a brilliant performance,” said the Arsenal manager.
Kylian Mbappé scored twice as Real Madrid overturned a half-time deficit to thrash PSV Eindhoven 5-1 and move three points clear at the top of the Champions League table overnight.
José Mourinho’s side trailed to Ivan Perisic’s 32nd-minute penalty, but Federico Valverde fired them level early in the second period. Jude Bellingham scored Real’s second with a sumptuous finish from outside the box and two clinical finishes from Mbappé extended his side’s 100% start to the competition this season to five matches before Vinícius Júnior (pictured congratulating Mbappé) added their fifth goal.
Como sit third in the table for now after securing their fourth win in the competition, 1-0 at home against AEK Athens , thanks to Luis Milla’s spectacular second-half winner. Lucas Da Cunha, the Como captain, missed a first-half penalty.
RB Leipzig notched their second win of the campaign as Antonio Nusa scored twice in a 3-1 home win over Lens and Melayro Bogarde’s stoppage-time own goal clinched Bodø/Glimt a 1-0 home win against Lask .
The Feyenoord midfielder Oussama Targhalline’s early own goal was enough to clinch Porto a 1-0 win in Rotterdam and Cucho Hernández scored twice as Real Betis won 2-0 at Slovan Bratislava . Press Association
Kobel managed to get his hand to a Tzolis effort that was heading for the top corner soon after, although Madueke should really have doubled Arsenal’s lead on the rebound. You began to wonder if Arsenal’s profligacy might cost them when Arrizabalaga was finally called into action on the stroke of half-time when he unconvincingly pushed Julian Ryerson’s cross out for a corner after a rare mistake from Declan Rice.
Arteta had more cause for concern at the start of the second half when a corner struck Gyökeres on the wrist, but the Italian referee waved away their protests.
There were groans at the other end when Martin Ødegaard passed up the opportunity to shoot after more good work from Madueke. That was made to look even more costly when Dortmund equalised with their next attack. The outstanding Joane Gadou stepped out of defence brilliantly to play in Beier and he made no mistake with his left foot. Clearly fancying his chances of a shock victory, Kovac threw on Konstantinos Karetsas and Serhou Guirassy as Arteta made a triple substitution. But Jurriën Timber’s first act was to give the ball away, with Bellingham denied moments later only by the assistant’s flag after Arrizabalaga had pushed Ryerson’s shot into his path.
The Dortmund goal led a charmed life in the final 20 minutes as Arsenal piled on the pressure. Only Guirassy will know how the ball managed to strike the post twice in the space of a second as he attempted to clear from a clever Ødegaard free-kick. Rice could not believe his luck when his effort struck a post with Kobel well beaten. But Dortmund stuck to their task and Arsenal had to learn the hard way again.

Arsenal dominate the chances as Borussia Dortmund fight back for a 1-1 draw in football’s Champions League.
Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres showed why he is such a polarising figure with a thunderous goal and a crucial miss in Tuesday’s 1-1 draw against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.
Gunners boss Mikel Arteta had urged Gyokeres to seize his opportunity after selecting the Swedish striker instead of Kai Havertz for the league phase tie at London’s Emirates Stadium.
Initially, Gyokeres looked like he was doing just that with his first goal at Emirates this season, and only his third for the Gunners in all competitions.
But the 28-year-old has been much maligned for his erratic displays since arriving from Sporting Lisbon in 2025.
And he gave more ammunition to his critics when he missed a golden opportunity to seal the points with a woeful header in the closing stages.
Dortmund had equalised through Maximilian Beier by then, and Arteta was left to rue his decision to put his faith in Gyokeres.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 11 games in all competitions, but this was not a vintage display by the English champions, who failed to win at home for the first time this season.
In a showdown between the current leaders of the Premier League and the Bundesliga, Arsenal were too profligate in attack and error-prone at the back to say they deserved all three points.
Arsenal sit fifth in the league phase with three wins and two draws from their five matches, while seventh-placed Dortmund are one point behind them.
Arteta will hope for a much more ruthless display in a significant Premier League showdown with spluttering title rivals Manchester City in north London on Sunday.
Arsenal were in control at the start, and Christos Tzolis’s strike bounced just over before Gyokeres tested Dortmund keeper Gregor Kobel with a long-range drive.
It was a warning Dortmund failed to heed as Gyokeres put Arsenal ahead in the 10th minute.
Fatally backing off when Gyokeres took possession 25 yards from goal, Dortmund’s defenders were punished by the Swede as he unleashed a superb dipping strike that flashed into the roof of the net.
Tzolis nearly doubled Arsenal’s lead with a curler that forced a sprawling save from Kobel.
Declan Rice almost replicated Gyokeres’s goal with a ferocious blast that fizzed just over.
Kepa Arrizabalaga was deputising for David Raya in goal for Arsenal after his fellow Spaniard suffered a shoulder injury in Saturday’s draw at Newcastle.
Such was Arsenal’s dominance that Kepa did not make a save until the final minute of the first half when he blocked Joane Gadou’s shot at the near post.
But Dortmund have a well-earned reputation as a stronger team in the second half this season, and they lived up to that tag once again.
Dortmund had a strong penalty appeal rejected after Gyokeres blocked a corner with his arm.
And with Arsenal unusually sloppy at the back, Dortmund’s pressure was rewarded in the 55th minute.
Gadou surged towards the Arsenal area before slipping a pass into Beier, who eluded Gabriel Magalhaes to plant a clinical low finish past Kepa.
Kobel saved Piero Hincapie’s close-range header as Arsenal tried to respond, while Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham had a goal disallowed for a tight offside.
Gyokeres wasted his chance to finish as Arsenal’s hero for once when he sent a close-range diving header woefully wide from Martin Odegaard’s cross.
Arsenal’s luck was out after Odegaard’s delivery twice hit the post and appeared to strike Serhou Guirassy’s hand before it was finally scrambled clear.
Rice was equally unfortunate with a first-time drive that cannoned back off the near post to leave Arsenal frustrated.

Ahead of Erdogan’s Libya trip, Haftar’s visit suggests Turkiye seeks another way to bring the country’s rivals together.
Eastern Libyan military commander Khalifa Haftar, flanked by his sons, arrived in Ankara on his first known visit to Turkiye, just days after a long-range Ukrainian attack struck a Russian ship in Benghazi.
Arriving on Tuesday to the Turkish capital, the Libyan commander was greeted by Turkish Chief of General Staff General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu at the airport, according to photos released by the General Command of the Libyan National Army (LNA).
There was no official media readout of the meeting, but Reuters news agency reported that Haftar is set to meet with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan.
Khaled and Belqasim Haftar accompanied their father to Ankara, according to the LNA’s General Command. Khaled is the LNA’s chief of staff, and Belqasim heads Libya’s Development and Reconstruction Fund.
Saddam Haftar, the LNA’s deputy commander and heir apparent, was in Doha for a separate meeting with Qatar’s minister of state for defence.
The visit came two days after Ukraine struck a Russian warship in Benghazi, the main city in Haftar-controlled eastern Libya, killing at least 10 Libyan and Russian crew members, according to local authorities.
The warship had docked to refuel and resupply under an agreement with the eastern authorities. Libya’s internationally recognised government in Tripoli condemned the attack on Monday, saying neither Russia nor Ukraine had the right to conduct military operations on Libyan territory or in its waters.
However, Turkish military support predates Ukraine’s long-range attack as Ankara helped the then-Tripoli government repel Haftar’s forces’ offensive in 2019 and 2020. Since a United Nations-brokered ceasefire ended major fighting in 2020, Turkiye has built ties with Haftar’s camp while maintaining its alliance with Tripoli.
On Saturday, Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan and intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met Abdul Hamid Dbeibah, prime minister of Libya’s Tripoli-based Government of National Unity, in Istanbul. Fidan later gave an interview to a Turkish television station, revealing Erdogan will visit Libya in December after a 15-year hiatus.
Khalifa Haftar’s visit to Ankara comes just weeks after Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives approved a 2019 maritime deal with Turkiye, reversing years of opposition, largely seen as an overture towards Turkiye as power-sharing talks in the country stall.
Khalifa Haftar’s son Saddam Haftar is reportedly eyeing the Libyan presidency role, backed by Washington.
Championed by Massad Boulos, United States President Donald Trump’s senior adviser for Arab and African affairs, the US is currently trying to broker a power-sharing proposal between Tripoli and Benghazi that would make Saddam Haftar the chairman of the Tripoli-based Presidency Council (PC).
Powerful factions in Tripoli and the western city of Misrata oppose giving Saddam the post, Jalel Harchaoui, a Libya analyst, told Al Jazeera.
“The Turks are more pragmatic and realistic than Boulos,” Harchaoui said. Ankara takes that opposition seriously, he said, because trying to force the appointment could destabilise Libya.
As Haftar pushes for the president role, approving the 2019 memorandum of understanding signed between Turkiye and Libya’s UN-recognised former Government of National Accord (GNA) on the delimitation of maritime boundaries between the two countries in the Mediterranean Sea was an effort to secure Ankara’s backing for the council chairmanship position, Harchaoui said.
The European Union condemned the vote, as did Greece, Israel and Egypt.
Despite Saddam Haftar’s absence from the Ankara meeting, by inviting his father, Harchaoui said, Erdogan has given himself another way to show progress in bringing Libya’s rivals together.
As Erdogan gears up for a visit to Libya, the Turkish president may seek a meeting between Dbeibah and Khalifa Haftar as Ankara’s effort to carve “a format of its own, calibrated to its own risk appetite and independent of the one Boulos has been pushing for months”, according to the analyst.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled Senegal to be the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations, which concluded in January; Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final but were stripped of the title in March, which led to their appeal
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has announced Senegal as the winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).
In response, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation said it was 'astonished' by the decision and 'affirms its intention to pursue all available legal procedures to appeal the decision'.
Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in January but were stripped of the title by a Confederation of African Football (CAF) appeal board in March for breaking competition rules by walking off the pitch because of a late disallowed goal and a controversial penalty awarded to their opponents.
Senegal's protest caused a delay of over 15 minutes and when their players returned to the pitch, Morocco's Brahim Diaz missed the penalty to force the match into extra time, with Pape Gueye going on to score the winner.
"The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025)," a CAS statement read.
"The decision rendered by the CAF appeal board is set aside and the decision by the CAF disciplinary board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal)."
Morocco's appeal was initially rejected but a CAF panel did uphold it and found Senegal's walk-off meant they had forfeited the match, awarding a 3-0 win to Morocco.
CAF said Senegal infringed on article 82 of AFCON's regulations, which states if a team refuses to play or leaves the ground before the end of regulation time without the referee's authorisation, it will be considered the loser and eliminated from the competition.
Article 84 states any team that violates article 82 will be permanently eliminated and lose the match 3-0.
However, the IFAB laws of the game state: "The decisions of the referee regarding facts connected with play, including whether or not a goal is scored and the result of the match, are final."
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Senegal appealed to CAS, calling the decision "a travesty", and have now been reinstated as champions.
The Moroccan federation wrote to the CAS earlier on Tuesday asking them to postpone the announcement of their decision. They wanted CAS to investigate allegations that one of the members of the CAS panel - Ulrich Haas - spoke on the telephone to the president of the Senegal FA Abdoulaye Fall on Sunday.
CAS confirmed it had received a challenge petition 'a few minutes' before the announcement but decided 'there were insufficient grounds at this stage to postpone the notification of the award'.
In April, IFAB - who are football's law makers - introduced a law stating that any players who leave the field of play in protest at a referee's decision can be sent off. The adoption of this law is at the discretion of the competition organiser.
"Common sense has prevailed because the Court of Arbitration for Sport have effectively confirmed that Senegal did win the 2025 AFCON.
"Morocco were very unhappy because they felt that the rules of the tournament had been broken by Senegal when they left the pitch. They felt that at that stage Senegal should have forfeited the game.
"They went to the African Confederation Appeal Board and there was an appeal hearing in March. That appeal decided that yes, Morocco were right and they should be the winners and the result of the game was changed from a 1-0 win to Senegal to a 3-0 win to Morocco.
"Then we had the next chapter in this story because Senegal were also very unhappy with the decision of the appeal board, so they went to CAS in Switzerland. There was a hearing in October and now we have had the decision - a unanimous decision from the three judges.
"I don't want to tempt fate, because let's wait and see what the Moroccan Federation say, but what I would say to you is that they have fought this all the way, they believe that this is an injustice and they are one of the most powerful football associations in Africa.
"They are co-hosts of the next World Cup in 2030 and they have a very close relationships with the leadership at FIFA.
"I'm not suggesting that anything untoward is going on, but they still do have options. For instance, if they feel there has been something wrong in the procedures at the CAS hearing, they could go to the Swiss Federal Tribunal.
"I think the Moroccan Federation, according to what Reuters are reporting this afternoon, are unhappy with the way CAS handled this appeal and they have complained to CAS because they believe that one of the judges actually spoke on the phone to the president of the Senegal Federation on Sunday afternoon, so perhaps that is an avenue that they are going to explore."
The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeal by the Senegalese Football Federation (FSF) against the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and the the Royal Moroccan Football Federation (FRMF, in French) concerning the final of the Africa Cup of Nations Morocco 2025 (AFCON 2025).
The decision rendered by the CAF Appeal Board is set aside and the decision by the CAF Disciplinary Board is reinstated. Consequently, the result obtained at the end of the AFCON 2025 final is confirmed (1-0 for Senegal).
The FSF appealed to CAS against a decision of the CAF Appeal Board declaring that the Senegal national team forfeited the AFCON 2025 final and recording the Moroccan national team as the winners.
In their appeal, the FSF argued that the decision of the Referee, Mr Jean-Jacques Ngambo Ndala, to resume the match at the 109th minute (90+19) during the AFCON 2025 final and to allow it to be concluded with a sporting result could not be reviewed, pursuant to the 'field of play' doctrine.
The FRMF argued, on the contrary, that the Referee's decision did not fall under the 'field of play' doctrine, as it cannot be applicable to the disciplinary consequences of the Senegalese team's behaviour. The FRMF alleged that, by leaving the pitch temporarily, the Senegalese team breached Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations, which should have led the Referee to bring the match to an early conclusion. The FRMF also argued that the Referee erred in law and that his decision was arbitrary.
After having examined the arguments raised by the Parties, the Arbitral Panel considered that the Referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority. By blowing his whistle to restart play, the Referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume.
In the Panel's view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee's decision were limited to the pitch. As such, the Panel considers that the Referee's decision was covered by the 'field of play' doctrine. Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team's conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case. In conclusion, the Panel considers that in resuming the match, the Referee did not err in law.
The Panel acknowledged that the Referee had to make a decision in an atmosphere of extreme tension. However, these circumstances do not justify describing the decision as "arbitrary". On the contrary, the Referee's judgment did not appear to have been affected by factors external to the game.
Regarding the disciplinary aspects of the case, the Panel noted that the FSF, the FSF coach Mr. Pape Thiaw, and certain players had already been sanctioned by CAF f…

texts.https://www.aljazeera.com/video/newsfeed: South Korea’s residents were urged to seek shelter as Russian military jets approached its airspace on Tuesday. But minutes later, the air raid alert was dropped. What happened?
texts.https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/24/sout:
South Korea scrambled fighter jets and told residents of an eastern island to take shelter on Tuesday after Russian air force aircraft came close to entering its territorial airspace, the military said.
The aircraft entered the Korea Air Defence Identification Zone and approached Ulleungdo island before turning away. The Joint Chiefs of Staff said no violation of South Korean territorial airspace occurred.
An air defence identification zone extends beyond national airspace and is used to identify approaching aircraft. Entering it does not by itself mean crossing into a country’s territorial airspace.
“Airspace intrusion was anticipated, therefore in order to protect the safety of our people, we issued a warning preemptively,” Jang Do-young, a spokesperson for the Joint Chiefs of Staff, told a briefing on Tuesday.
The interior ministry issued the shelter warning at around 7:52 am local time (11:52 pm CET Monday), telling residents to move underground or inside buildings. It was lifted within minutes.
Conflicting messages added to the confusion. The initial alert said Russian aircraft had entered South Korean airspace. A later message from North Gyeongsang provincial authorities misidentified the aircraft as possibly North Korean. The military clarified that they were Russian and had remained outside territorial airspace.
South Korean news agency Yonhap reported that the aircraft spent about 20 minutes inside the identification zone. It said this was the first time South Korea’s military had issued a precautionary civilian alert over a possible airspace violation by Russian warplanes.
South Korea’s defence ministry summoned Russia’s military attaché Colonel Nikolai Marchenko later on Tuesday to protest and demand measures to prevent a repeat.
The ministry said repeated unannounced entries into the identification zone and the latest close approach could unnecessarily raise tensions on the Korean Peninsula and across the region.
The foreign ministry also conveyed its objections to Moscow through diplomatic channels, Yonhap reported.
Poland also reported a brief Russian drone incursion late on Monday. Polish officials said the aircraft turned east and that forces had decided against shooting it down because of the potential risk to civilians.
That followed an incident on Friday in which three Russian Kh-101 missiles landed in Poland, according to Polish prosecutors.
NATO has authorised the deployment of an airborne early-warning aircraft to Poland in response to the missile incident, an alliance spokesperson confirmed on Monday. The aircraft uses radar to detect and track activity over a wide area.
Japan separately scrambled fighter jets last Thursday after two aircraft believed to be Russian briefly entered its territorial airspace near Okinoshima, off Fukuoka. Tokyo lodged a diplomatic protest with Moscow.

Nato chief Mark Rutte and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz respond to reports of Russian plans to launch nuclear weapons into space
Nato chief Mark Rutte has said the alliance will defend against any threats in space after German reports that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite.
Intelligence reports about a possible launch in the next 60 days had been shared among Nato countries this month, according to German media. It was not clear which country had authored the reports.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said such reports were "not new, yet they remain no less shocking", and a government spokesman said the reports were being taken "very seriously".
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said he had not seen the reports but dismissed stories citing "unknown sources" as "hardly worth taking seriously".
The Russian embassy in Berlin told German media it rejected what it called "unfounded allegations" and said the reports were part of a "propaganda campaign".
Citing anonymous German military and intelligence sources, public broadcasters NDR and WDR and newspaper Süddeutscher Zeitung, said the Russian satellite was dubbed "Sputnik-S" and was equipped with a nuclear warhead. It could be used to disrupt or destroy other satellites, including important communication and observation satellites.
Asked about the reports, the Nato secretary general told a press conference in Berlin alongside Merz: "We will always make sure we defend every inch of Nato territory, and that includes making sure we are safe when it comes to the space element."
The Western defensive alliance had a variety of response options, said Rutte.
"When it comes to the military domain, we will always make assessments of our deterrence and defence and make updates where necessary."
Merz did not confirm or deny the reports of Russia's plans, but said they "reveal the level of escalation Russia is evidently prepared to pursue".
German government spokesman Stefan Kornelius warned against causing "excessive nervousness regarding hypothetical dangers".
Josef Aschbacher, the head of the European Space Agency, told the Handeslblatt newspaper that having nuclear weapons in space was "the ultimate nightmare scenario".
Russia is a signatory to the 1967 Outer Space Treaty, which bans weapons of mass destruction from orbit.
Bleddyn Bowen, co-director of the Space Research Centre at Durham University, said that exploding a nuclear weapon in space would have "massive infrastructural effects" as there were now more than 15,000 active satellites. But he told the BBC's Today programme that "the effect of these weapons would be extremely indiscriminate and also take out a lot of Russia's own space infrastructure".
Other countries, including the US and China, have deployed or plan to deploy other weapons in space, exploring other capabilities outside of the treaty, such as targeting rivals' satellites - which are key for military communications, surveillance and navigation.
In 2024 the US accused Russia of developing a "space-based" anti-satellite weapon armed with a nuclear warhead. Russia denied the accusation .
"Our position is clear and transparent. We have always been categorically against the deployment of nuclear weapons in space and we are still against it," President Vladimir Putin said at the time.
In September the US Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said the US had "on-orbit, space-control weapons" circling the planet, but did not provide specifics. In response to the announcement, the Kremlin's Peskov told Russian media that space "must be free of any weapon".

Landmine monitor found 84 percent of deaths caused by landmines were in Southeast Asia.
Casualties from landmines or unexploded ordnance reached a five-year high in 2025, with the largest number of deaths recorded in Southeast Asia, largely driven by Myanmar’s civil war.
A report by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines found civilians were the most affected, making up some 84 percent of the 6,929 casualties recorded in 2025, half of them were children.
In Myanmar, where both the government and armed groups are using landmines, 1,891 deaths were recorded in 2025, the highest number of any country for the third consecutive year.
On average, five people are killed or wounded by landmines daily in Myanmar, the report found.
“Myanmar has gone beyond crisis to catastrophe, and has claimed the ignoble title of top producer of landmine victims for a third year in a row,” said Yeshua Moser-Puangsuwan, a co-author of the Landmine Monitor 2026 report.
“There is now contamination at some level in almost two-thirds of the townships of the country.”
Myanmar – along with Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and other countries in the region – accounted for 27 percent of global deaths from landmines in 2025, despite having only 8 percent of the world’s population.
Syria saw a spike of more than 50 percent in casualties, with 1,602 deaths recorded in 2025 after large numbers of civilians returned after the fall of ousted President Bashar al-Assad in 2024.
“Syria is huge, but it is a post-war crisis,” Moser-Puangsuwan said. “People are now returning, and that is driving the casualty figure. They need to radically scale up their clearance capacity.”
The International Campaign to Ban Landmines has been urging more countries to join the 1997 Mine Ban Treaty to end stockpiling, production and the transfer of antipersonnel mines.
Despite this, five countries on the borders with Russia – Finland, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania and Poland – pulled out of the treaty, citing the “security situation in our region”.
Ukraine, meanwhile, notified the United Nations that it had decided to suspend the implementation of the treaty, even though such a move is not allowed under its provisions.
Russia, not a party to the treaty, has been making widespread use of mines in its invasion of Ukraine, and Landmine Monitor found that Ukraine had been using them as well.
Lebanon, the Marshall Islands and Tonga all joined the Mine Ban Treaty during the reporting period, and 162 countries are now bound by it.

Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife Carla Bruni-Sarkozy are to face trial next year over charges stemming from the former French president's conviction for conspiring to fund his election campaign with money from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi.
The charges centre on the retraction of the testimony of a key witness who had initially said he had evidence that could incriminate Sarkozy.
Sarkozy was given a five-year sentence in the case last September and became the first French ex-president to go to jail, even though he only spent 20 days behind bars. He has always denied doing anything wrong in the case and the appeals verdict is expected next Monday.
Since losing his re-election bid in 2012, Sarkozy has faced several criminal investigations.
In 2024, he was handed a one-year sentence – of which six months were suspended – over the illegal financing of his 2012 re-election campaign.
In 2021, he was found guilty of trying to bribe a judge and sentenced to three years in jail – two of them suspended – and thus became the first former French president to get a custodial sentence. He was allowed to serve his time at home wearing a tag instead of going to jail.
The new case centres on a Libyan businessman, Ziad Takieddine, who had said he had written proof that Sarkozy's 2007 campaign bid was "abundantly" financed by Tripoli, and that the €50m (£43m) in payments continued after he became president.
Takieddine, who died last year, withdrew his accusations in an interview in 2020.
At the time, Sarkozy was said to have stated: the "truth is finally coming out", but officials found the retraction to be "insincere" and a new investigation was launched into the "Save Sarko" file – the nickname the alleged perpetrators had used for the operation, according to French media.
So the former head of state and his wife, an Italian-born former supermodel and singer, will now face charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" and benefiting from witness tampering. They deny any wrongdoing.

A hack of Russia's federal statistics agency Rosstat has revealed that at least 490,000 Russian military personnel have been killed in Ukraine since the start of Moscow's full-scale invasion in February 2022, according to data obtained by hackers and analysed by multiple independent news outlets.
Two hacking groups, Cyber Partisans of Belarus and Silent Crow — which also carried out a 2025 attack on Aeroflot's servers — extracted the data in a breach on the night of 1 November.
The hackers accessed Rosstat's electronic document management system and database, which contains around 23 terabytes of statistical, economic and personal data, including census materials.
The figure of at least 490,000 deaths derives from official death certificates registered between February 2022 and the end of August 2026.
Meduza, applying actuarial and epidemiological modelling to the data, estimated at least 720,000 irrecoverable losses when it includes those missing in action. Rosstat's documents alone cannot capture the full toll, as the database does not include servicemen whose deaths have not yet been registered.
Researchers and journalists justify including the missing in total loss figures because, according to Mediazona, confirmed survival is recorded in fewer than 10% of missing servicemen cases.
Under current battlefield conditions, with drone warfare making the evacuation of bodies increasingly difficult, the death tally is likely to grow.
Deaths are also registered with an average delay of 3.5 months, and those of missing soldiers with a delay of about a year, Novaya Evropa reported.
Using the conservative estimate of 490,000 to 500,000 dead, Russia sustained an average of 280 to 300 fatalities a day — one death every five minutes — according to Important Stories, which examined the leak alongside more than a dozen other independent outlets.
The outlet found that 92% of Russian servicemen died from explosions and shrapnel, with firearms accounting for only 1.3% of deaths. The Insider identified more than 370,000 of the dead by name.
The BBC Russian Service and Mediazona said at least 7,421 foreigners have been killed fighting on Russia's side.
Journalists also analysed deaths among Russian servicemen from non-combat causes. Around 2,500 died as a result of alcohol and drug use or suicide.
According to confidential Rosstat data analysed by the international news outlets, more than 1,000 Russian servicemen took their own lives since the start of the invasion.
The deaths of another 885 soldiers in Ukraine or near its borders were registered as firearm injuries "with undetermined intent," a classification experts believe is used in some cases to conceal suicides.
Together, the two figures represent a number comparable to a full Russian regiment.
Military analysts note the problem is deepened in the Russian armed forces by intense pressure from fellow soldiers and commanders, fear of assignment to high-casualty fighting areas known as "meatgrinder assaults," and contracts that in practice prevent soldiers from leaving the war.
The number of Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine is the highest in Russia's Far East and Siberia relative to their populations.
Russia's Jewish Autonomous Region in the Far East recorded nearly 1,000 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, Zabaykalsky around 800, Chukotka 760 and Tuva 650.
Moscow, which the authorities have worked to insulate from the visible effects of the war, recorded 63 deaths per 100,000 inhabitants, according to Important Stories.
The Kremlin does not publish or recognise figures for Russian losses from the invasion. Russian authorities have restricted access to official databases and prosecuted those conducting independent counts.
Ukraine's General Staff estimated Russia's losses since February 2022 at 1,639,641 servicemen, encompassing both killed and wounded, although the figure has not been independently verified.
The Economist, in a study published at the end of October, put the number of Russian servicemen killed at between 374,000 and 770,000, and total losses including the wounded at between 1.4 and 2.1 million.
The Ukrainian armed forces' General Staff reported that October of this year was the bloodiest month for Russia since the invasion began.
The Insider said the Russian armed forces suffered their heaviest losses in spring 2025, during fighting on the Pokrovsk axis, when more than 61,000 were killed over three months.

Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund. UEFA Champions League Round 1.
Match report as Arsenal are denied victory by Borussia Dortmund in a Champions League encounter at the Emirates Stadium; Viktor Gyokeres scored a spectacular opener but Maximilian Beier equalised as the Gunners wasted a string of chances
Arsenal were punished for failing to take their chances for the second game in a row as Maximilian Beier clinched a 1-1 draw for Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.
Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal an early lead with a stunning strike from distance but the game followed a similar pattern to Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle as they were unable to capitalise on a one-sided first half before conceding after the break.
Dortmund's leveller came when Beier slotted a clinical finish past Kepa Arrizabalaga, standing in for the injured David Raya, following a rampaging run from defender Joane Gadou.
Arsenal racked up 30 shots and had a string of chances to win it in the closing stages, hitting the woodwork through Jurrien Timber's deflected cut-back and again through Declan Rice's low shot.
Gyokeres also spurned opportunities, firing over from close range from Martin Odegaard's pass shortly before half-time, then heading awkwardly wide from a few yards out when it looked easier to score from another Odegaard ball.
Dortmund had dangerous moments too, including a Jobe Bellingham goal ruled out for offside and a penalty appeal for a handball by Gyokeres following a corner.
Arsenal remain unbeaten in the Champions League but the draw causes them to drop two places in the league phase table to fifth before they resume their Premier League campaign at home to Manchester City, live on Sky Sports on Sunday.
Arsenal's total of 30 shots was their highest in the Champions League either this season or last. But only one of them ended up in the net. Only four of them were even on target.
There were clear parallels with Saturday's game at St James' Park. Again, Arsenal were outstanding in the first half. Again, though, they reached the interval with only one goal to show for their efforts.
Dortmund, like Newcastle, came out with renewed belief, and a lot more intensity. Even before Beier's equaliser, the same player had missed a glorious chance when he failed to connect with a Joey Veerman cross. Arsenal were suddenly on the back foot.
They regained control after Dortmund's leveller, albeit while avoiding a scare when Jobe Bellingham had a goal ruled out for offside. But their attempts to break down the visitors were unsuccessful. Good positions were wasted. They should have been out of sight.
Arteta couldn't believe it when the otherwise impressive Gyokeres skewed his header wide from Odegaard's cross. The Arsenal boss was on his knees when Timber's cut-back ricocheted off the post.
It is positive that they are creating so many chances. Their performance featured another bright showing from Noni Madueke. But they will need to find some cutting edge against City.
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta : "I think it was a brilliant performance.
"The way we played, bearing in mind the opposition that we played today, is something to be very, very pleased about.
"There is very little more that you can demand from the team.
"But obviously there is the feeling that we should reward ourselves much more when you put that kind of performance, with the amount of chances and situations.
"There is an element of luck and there is an element of us finishing the actions better. We need to insist, because I think what the team has done and shown today is the right direction.
"I love the way the team played. I think there's no question how superior, how dominant, how much of a threat we were, how connected everybody was to the game. It was great to watch.
"It was unbelievable that sometimes the ball hasn't ended up in the back of the net. That's my feeling."
Borussia Dortmund boss Niko Kovac : "I thought VAR should have looked at the handball. It would have been worth a check.
"They are trying to intervene less, but it doesn't mean you should not intervene when you should do.
"In such a situation, you have to at least have someone in the VAR room saying, 'Let's just look at it.'
"I am not crying about it. It is what it is. We got a point. It is a big point away to Arsenal, a big one for all of us, our fans, our team, and the club."

Eski Fransa Cumhurbaşkanı Nicolas Sarkozy'nin Libya davası etrafında yeni bir yargı süreci başladı. Paris'teki soruşturma hakimleri bu kez davanın kilit tanığıyla ilgili bir karar verdi. Kararda Sarkozy'nin yanı sıra eşi Carla Bruni-Sarkozy'nin de adı geçiyor. Dosyada toplam 11 kişi bulunuyor ve yargılamanın takvimi de belli oldu.
Paris'teki soruşturma hakimleri, Sarkozy ve eşi Carla Bruni-Sarkozy'nin de aralarında olduğu 11 kişinin gelecek yıl mahkeme karşısına çıkmasına karar verdi. Çift 3 Kasım ile 2 Aralık 2027 arasında 'suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurmak' ve 'tanığı manipüle etme' suçlamalarıyla yargılanacak. Ulusal basındaki haberlere göre karar, Libya davasında tanık statüsündeki iş insanı Ziad Takieddine'in Sarkozy hakkındaki ifadesini değiştirmesiyle ilgili yürütülen soruşturmada çıktı.
Fransız-Lübnan kökenli iş insanı Takieddine, önce Sarkozy'nin Libya'dan finansman aldığını savunmuş, 2020'de ifadelerini değiştirerek aksini iddia etmişti. Soruşturmada Sarkozy'nin, Takieddine'in kendisi hakkındaki suçlamaları çekmesi için farklı kişiler aracılığıyla baskı yapıp yapmadığı, yani hukuk dışı yöntemlere başvurup başvurmadığı araştırılıyordu. 75 yaşındaki Takieddine, 23 Eylül 2025'te Lübnan'ın başkenti Beyrut'ta hayatını kaybetmişti.
Fransa 'da 2007-2012 döneminde cumhurbaşkanlığı yapan Sarkozy'nin, 2007 seçim kampanyasını yürütmek için dönemin Libya lideri Muammer Kaddafi'den yasa dışı maddi destek aldığı ileri sürülmüştü. Takieddine'in de 2006 sonlarında Libya'dan Sarkozy'ye 5 milyon avro getirdiği iddia edilmişti. İddiaların ardından 2013'te olayla ilgili soruşturma açıldı ve yargı süreci kamuoyunda 'Libya davası' olarak anılmaya başladı.
Paris Ceza Mahkemesi, 25 Eylül 2025'te görülen Libya davasında Sarkozy'yi pasif yolsuzluk, kamu fonlarını zimmete geçirmeyi gizleme ve yasa dışı kampanya finansmanı suçlarından beraat ettirmiş, suç örgütü kurmaktan ise 5 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırmıştı. Sarkozy karara itiraz etse de kararın niteliği gereği temyiz süreci sonuçlanmadan hapse girmesi kesinleşti. Eski Cumhurbaşkanı 21 Ekim 2025'te cezaevine girdi ve 20 gün sonra adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakıldı. Temyiz kararı için gözler şimdi 30 Kasım'a çevrildi.

Gündemi BBC Türkçe'den takip etmek artık WhatsApp'ta da mümkün. Haberlerimizin doğrudan telefonunuza gelmesi için tıklayın.
Eski Fransa cumhurbaşkanı Nicolas Sarkozy ve eşi Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, dönemin Libya lideri Muammer Kaddafi'nin 2007'de Fransa'daki seçim kampanyasına usulsüz şekilde mali destek sağladığı iddialarıyla ilgili gelecek yıl yargılanacak.
Suçlamaların merkezinde, Sarkozy'nin suçlanabileceği delillere sahip olduğunu söyleyen kilit bir tanığın ifadesini geri çekmesi var.
Sarkozy, Eylül 2025'te aynı davada beş yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılmış ve hapse giren ilk Fransız eski cumhurbaşkanı olmuştu.
Eski cumhurbaşkanı dava boyunca hakkındaki suçlamaları her zaman reddetti.
Başvurduğu temyiz kararının da önümüzdeki hafta açıklanması bekleniyor.
Sarkozy, 2012'deki seçimle iktidarı kaybetmesinden bu yana farklı soruşturmalarla karşı karşıya kaldı.
Şubat 2024'te, 2012'deki seçim kampanyasında fazla para harcamak ve bunu örtmek için bir halkla ilişkiler şirketi kurmaktan suçlu bulundu.
Altı ayı ertelenen bir yıllık hapis cezası alan Sarkozy, kararı temyize götürdü.
2021'de, 2015'te bir yargıca rüşvet vermeye çalışmaktan suçlu bulundu ve üç yıl hapis cezası aldı, iki yılı ertelendi.
Paris'teki temyiz mahkemesi Sarkozy'nin hapse girmek yerine evde elektronik kelepçe kullanarak cezasını tamamlamasına izin verdi.
Yeni dava, Libyalı iş insanı Ziad Takieddine'nin yazılı kanıtı olduğu yönündeki iddiasına dayanıyor.
Bu iddiaya göre, Sarkozy'nin 2007 seçim kampanyası Trablus tarafından "bol miktarda" finanse edildi ve ödemeler o cumhurbaşkanı olduktan sonra da devam etti.
Geçen yıl hayatını kaybeden Takieddine, 2020'de verdiği bir röportajda suçlamalarını geri çekmişti.
O dönemde Sarkozy'nin "gerçek nihayet ortaya çıkıyor" dediği söyleniyordu.
Fransız medyasına göre, iddia edilen faillerin operasyon için kullandığı takma ad olan "Sarko'yu Kurtar" dosyası hakkında yeni bir soruşturma başlatıldı.
Eski devlet başkanı ile eski süper model ve şarkıcı olan eşi Carla Bruni, şimdi "organize bir grubun parçası olarak dolandırıcılık yapmak için suç ortaklığı kurmak ve tanıkların ifadelerini etkilemekle ilgili çalıntı malları kabul etmek" suçlamalarıyla karşı karşı.
Orijinali İngilizce olan bu makalenin çevirisinde yapay zekadan yararlandık. Yayınlanmadan önce çeviriyi bir BBC gazetecisi kontrol etti. Yapay zekayı nasıl kullandığımız hakkında daha fazla bilgi burada .

Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığına bağlı İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi, Anadolu’nun tarihi ve kültürel zenginliğini çağdaş opera anlayışıyla Atatürk Kültür Merkezi sahnesine taşıyor.
Bestesi Güldiyar Tanrıdağlı’ya, librettosu Prof. Dr. İskender Pala’ya ait eser; Lidya Krallığı’nın son döneminde yaşanan siyasi mücadeleleri, Pers tehdidini ve insan ilişkilerini müziğin anlatım gücüyle izleyiciye aktaracak.

Rejisör Caner Akın tarafından sahneye konulan eser, geleneksel opera anlatımını çağdaş ve deneysel sahneleme teknikleriyle buluşturuyor.
Dekor, kostüm, ışık ve video tasarımlarıyla zenginleşen prodüksiyon, Lidya’nın tarihsel dünyasını günümüz sahnesine taşırken izleyicilere görsel ve müzikal bir deneyim sunuyor.
İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Orkestrasını İbrahim Yazıcı’nın yöneteceği prodüksiyonun dekor ve görsel tasarımını Efter Tunç, kostüm tasarımını Olcay Engin Kaymaz, ışık tasarımını Cem Yılmazer, video tasarımını Aisha Hajiyeva, koreografisini ise Berk Sarıbay üstleniyor. İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Korosu’nu Anıl Aydın hazırlıyor.
Eserde Edusa karakterini dönüşümlü olarak Gülbin Günay ve Evren Işık Yasemin canlandıracak. Halludas rolünde Mert Süngü ve Ufuk Toker, Krezüs rolünde Göktuğ Alpaşar ve Gökhan Ürben, Namirek rolünde Nesrin Gönüldağ ve Asude Karayavuz, Kyros rolünde Yoel Keşap ve Hüseyin Likos, Solon rolünde Caner Akgün ve Kevork Tavityan, Karuna rolünde Barbora Hitay ve Deniz Likos sahne alacak.
Eserin geniş sanatçı kadrosunda Berk Dalkılıç, Bülent Külekçi, Alper Göçeri, Murat Güney, Kenan Dağaşan, Emre Güngör, Burak Kul, Talip Savranbaşı, Arda Durgut, Ufuk Karakoç, Efe Doğrukul, Bahadır Özkoca, Uğur Etiler, Okan Fidan, Mehmet Tükel Acar, Fuat Kılıç Aslan ve Mehmet Eminhan Turgut’un yanı sıra İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi bale ve modern dans sanatçıları da yer alacak.
Geçtiğimiz sezon dünya prömiyeri gerçekleştirilen ve İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi repertuvarında yerini alan “Edusa”, 26 ve 28 Kasım ile 10 ve 12 Aralık 2026 tarihlerinde Atatürk Kültür Merkezi Türk Telekom Opera Salonu’nda sanatseverlerle buluşacak.

In recent days, Ukraine has sunk a Russian warship docked in port in Libya, and Russian missiles have landed in Poland. The Kremlin has not commented on the missiles.
MICHEL MARTIN, HOST: Depending on your point of view, Russia's war in Ukraine is either revving up or winding down. STEVE INSKEEP, HOST: This month, the Trump administration claimed it was making progress toward a negotiated peace. Also this month, the fighting has expanded geographically into Eastern Europe, Northern Europe, even the Mediterranean, as if it was a world war. MARTIN: Joining us to talk about both these dynamics is NPR's Charles Maynes from Moscow. Charles, good morning. CHARLES MAYNES, BYLINE: Morning, Michel. MARTIN: So Russia and Ukraine are both striking out far beyond their borders. How concerned should we be? MAYNES: You know, there have been long concerns that an incident along NATO's northeastern flank near a border in Russia could serve as a tripwire for turning the war in Ukraine into a wider conflict. But recent events have brought that back to our attention. Last week we saw three Russian cruise missiles land in southeastern Poland, and on Saturday, a sanctioned Russian cargo ship was hit by what is presumed to have been a Ukrainian drone in the Baltic Sea. But now we're also seeing action further afield. Ukraine destroyed a Russian naval warship docked in Libya in the Mediterranean. Russia has its own shadow role providing intel to Iran in its war with the U.S. And just this morning, South Korea said it scrambled jets to chase away Russian sorties operating near its airspace. So the spillover is real, and the map is wide. MARTIN: So what is being done to contain it? MAYNES: Well, you know, Russian President Vladimir Putin constantly dismisses this idea that he's seeking direct confrontation with NATO. He says it's absurd. But there have been a spate of recent incidents of bomb threats, cyberattacks, sabotage that some in Europe believe are the work of Russia's security services. Russia's goal, it seems, would be to tear at the alliance's core commitment to collective security - this idea that an attack on one is an attack on all - and it's divided NATO. How do you respond to acts that fall below this threshold of outright war? So for example, President Trump has dismissed incursions by Russia into NATO airspace as basically mistakes. Now, as to other areas where we've seen Ukraine launch attacks, like Libya or apparently the Baltic Sea, it seems to show that Ukraine is intent on striking symbols of Russian power anywhere, and that also makes some supporters of Kyiv nervous. MARTIN: On the diplomatic front, President Trump is suggesting that a peace deal may be in the offing. Why does he say that? MAYNES: Well, after two years, we saw the Trump administration really make no headway. They've changed tactics by expanding the talks beyond Russia and Ukraine to focus on European security as a whole. And the conversations are now fundamentally centered on what security guarantees are on offer to Ukraine, to Russia, and to Europe. But the problem seems to be there's a bit of a disconnect between what that means to each of them. For example, Trump's envoys say Russia is, quote, "comfortable" with NATO-like guarantees for Ukraine. Russian officials have pushed back against that idea hard. But President Trump - he says this is all public posturing, that everyone is being much more flexible behind the scenes. We'll just have to see if he's right. MARTIN: And meanwhile, the war continues. MAYNES: It does, and it was staggering losses, particularly from the Russian side, if new findings published yesterday by various independent Russian media in exile is correct. They've been sifting through data that was hacked from Russia's statistics agency and concluded that upwards of an astonishing 700,000 Russian troops have been killed in this war, and those numbers continue to grow. MARTIN: That is NPR's Charles Maynes in Moscow. Charles, thank you. MAYNES: Thank you.

France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. The new charges are related to the Sarkozy couple's actions during the case examining illegal campaign funding from Libyan strongman Muammar Gaddafi over which Sarkozy was imprisoned last year.
France 's ex-president Nicolas Sarkozy , his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy , and a paparazzi boss will stand trial next year over alleged witness tampering in a case over funding for his 2007 election, a source close to the case said Tuesday.
France's right-wing leader from 2007 to 2012 has been embroiled in legal woes since leaving office.
Last year he became modern France's first former president to go to jail over seeking illegal campaign funding from late Libyan dictator Muammar Gaddafi in exchange for help restoring his international image.
Read more Ex-president Sarkozy’s 20-day prison diary: ‘Like the Count of Monte Cristo’?
The former head of state was freed from jail after 20 days pending his appeal, and an appeals court is to issue its ruling on Monday.
One of the main accusers in the case was French-Lebanese businessman Ziad Takieddine , who died in Lebanon last year.
In 2016 he claimed he helped deliver up to €5 million ($6 million) in cash from Gaddafi to Sarkozy and the former president's chief of staff in 2006 and 2007.
But in November 2020, Takieddine suddenly retracted his incriminating statement in an interview with French media.
Read more Key Lebanese-French accuser in Sarkozy Libya funding probe dies on eve of verdict
This prompted accusations that Sarkozy and his wife enlisted the help of paparazzi queen Mimi Marchand to pay the witness to change his mind, something they have always denied.
Bruni is suspected of having requested a clandestine phone line in late 2019 to communicate with Marchand about the Takieddine operation.
A court will in November next year try Sarkozy and Bruni on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering, the source told AFP.
Marchand stands accused of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as witness tampering.
Their lawyers did not immediately respond to an AFP request for comment.
The defendants face a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison and a fine of €150,000.
Sarkozy has received two definitive convictions in other cases – linked to overspending in his failed 2012 re-election bid, and later trying to extract favours from a judge.
Marchand was last year handed an 18-month suspended prison sentence for blackmailing a television host, who feared the paparazzi boss would publish images of her daughter leaving police custody.

Galatasaray Başkanı Dursun Özbek'ten dikkat çeken bir açıklama geldi. Özbek, Habertürk 'e yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, taraftarların RAMS Park tribünlerinde Filistin'e destek için açtığı pankartlar nedeniyle İsrail'deki Netanyahu hükümetinin kulübü UEFA'ya şikayet ettiğini duyduklarını söyledi. Özbek, sarı-kırmızılıların duruşunun siyasi değil, insani ve vicdani olduğunu vurguladı.
Habertürk 'ün aktardığına göre Özbek, açıklamasına İsrail hükümetinin girişimini duyduklarını söyleyerek başladı. Galatasaray Başkanı'na göre şikayetin gerekçesi, sarı-kırmızılı taraftarların iç saha maçlarında tribünlerde Filistin halkına destek amacıyla açtığı pankartlar.
Açıklama, Galatasaray'ın Şampiyonlar Ligi 'nde Aston Villa ile karşılaşmaya hazırlandığı günlerde geldi. Şikayetin ne zaman ve hangi maçlar gerekçe gösterilerek yapıldığına dair ayrıntı paylaşılmadı. UEFA ve İsrail tarafından da konuya ilişkin bir açıklama gelmedi.
Özbek, açıklamasında Türk milletinin tarih boyunca olduğu gibi bugün de mazlumun yanında durmaya devam edeceğini söyledi. Galatasaray Başkanı, Filistin halkının yaşadığı acılara sessiz kalmayacaklarını da ekledi.
Özbek'e göre dünyanın dört bir yanında Filistin halkının maruz kaldığı zulme karşı ortak bir vicdani ses yükseliyor. Bu da tribünlerdeki desteğin siyasi bir mesaj değil, insani ve vicdani bir duruş olduğunu gösteriyor.
Açıklamanın son bölümünde UEFA'ya seslenen Özbek, kurumun bu hassasiyeti aynı anlayışla değerlendirmesini ve siyasi saiklerle yapıldığını düşündükleri şikayete itibar etmemesini umduklarını söyledi.
Özbek'e göre futbolu siyasetten uzak tutmanın yolu, insani ve vicdani duruşları cezalandırmak değil; futbolun siyasi baskılara konu edilmesinin önüne geçmek.
UEFA'nın şikayeti işleme alıp almayacağı ve Galatasaray hakkında bir disiplin süreci başlatıp başlatmayacağı ise henüz belli değil.

Spoiler warning: This story reveals details of The Great British Bake Off final
Moyin Odeniran said he was "in shock" after being crowned the winner of the 17th series of The Great British Bake Off.
The 22-year-old from Loughton, Essex, described it as a "very busy time" as he juggled competing in the Channel 4 baking competition with completing his university studies .
Despite his dissertation being due a month after filming wrapped, Odeniran achieved a first in his political economy degree at King's College London.
He beat fellow finalists Tom Whittaker, from West Yorkshire, and Birmingham student Mo Mahir to the title in Tuesday night's episode.
"I don't know how that happened, I don't know how I got here. I can't believe it – I am in shock," the talented baker said.
"I have made friends for life and I have just loved every single second of it, and I don't think I could have asked for anything more."
Judge Paul Hollywood described Odeniran's efforts as "pure magic" after watching his jubilant celebrations with family and friends.
"He has done an amazing job because out of all the bakers he struggled at the beginning, and he actually got better and better," Hollywood said.
Fellow judge Nigella Lawson praised Odeniran as a "worthy winner", but also said the other finalists were "sensational".
The high-stakes final saw the three contestants tasked with making a citrus celebration cake, creme brulee donuts and a "spectacular tribute to iconic British landscapes".
Reflecting on his performance in the final, Odeniran said: "I didn't want to put too much pressure on myself, but I knew I had put my best foot forward.
"I couldn't have done anything better than I did and I had a great time doing it."
He said he got "quite exhausted" while filming the series and praised his mother, sister and close friends for their support.
"Earlier on, some of the challenges were quite difficult for me and I was shocked that I kept going through," Odeniran said.
"Before you get there you think you know how to bake, and by week two you question whether you know anything about baking."
He shared his gratitude at being able to learn from Lawson and Hollywood.
"I will never forget my time there and the friendships made which will always continue," the winner added.
Prior to the final, Odeniran told BBC Essex he planned to view it at a huge "watch party" at his local church .

Fransa ulusal basındaki haberlere göre, Libya davasında "tanık" statüsündeki iş insanı Ziad Takieddine'in, Sarkozy hakkındaki ifadesini değiştirmesiyle ilgili yürütülen soruşturmada yeni bir gelişme oldu.
Paris'teki soruşturma hakimleri, Sarkozy ve eşi Bruni-Sarkozy'nin de aralarında olduğu 11 kişinin gelecek yıl mahkeme karşısına çıkmasına karar verdi.
Bu kapsamda, Sarkozy ve eşi Bruni-Sarkozy, 3 Kasım-2 Aralık 2027 tarihlerinde "suç işlemek amacıyla örgüt kurmak" ve "tanığı manipüle etme" suçlarından yargılanacak.
AA'nın haberine göre, soruşturma kapsamında, Sarkozy'nin, Libya dosyasında "kilit tanık" statüsündeki Takieddine'in kendisi hakkındaki ifadesini 2020'de değiştirmesi için hukuk dışı yöntemlere başvurup başvurmadığı araştırılıyordu.
Öte yandan, Sarkozy'nin yargılandığı Libya davasına ilişkin temyiz kararının 30 Kasım'da çıkması bekleniyor.
Fransa'da 2007-2012 döneminde cumhurbaşkanı olan Sarkozy'nin, "2007'de cumhurbaşkanlığı seçim kampanyasını yürütmek için dönemin Libya lideri Muammer Kaddafi'den yasa dışı maddi destek aldığı" ileri sürülmüştü.
Fransız-Lübnan kökenli Takieddine'nin de 2006 sonlarında Libya'dan Sarkozy'ye 5 milyon avro getirdiği iddia edilmişti.
İddiaların ardından 2013'te olayla ilgili soruşturma açılmış ve kamuoyunda "Libya davası" olarak adlandırılan yargı süreci başlamıştı.
İş insanı Takieddine de önce Sarkozy'nin Libya'dan finansman aldığını savunmuş, 2020'de ifadelerini değiştirerek aksini iddia etmişti.
Sarkozy'nin Takieddine'ye, kendisi hakkında suçlamaları çekmesi için farklı kişiler aracılığıyla baskı yaptığından şüpheleniliyor.
75 yaşındaki Takieddine, 23 Eylül 2025'te Lübnan'ın başkenti Beyrut'ta hayatını kaybetmişti.
Paris Ceza Mahkemesi, 25 Eylül 2025'te görülen Libya davasında, Sarkozy'nin "pasif yolsuzluk, kamu fonlarını zimmete geçirmeyi gizleme ve yasa dışı kampanya finansmanı" suçlarından beraatine, "suç örgütü kurmak" suçundan ise 5 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılmasına karar vermişti.
Sarkozy, karara itiraz etse de mahkeme kararının niteliği gereği temyiz süreci sonuçlanmadan hapse girmesi kesinleşmişti.
Fransa'da 21 Ekim 2025'te cezaevine giren eski Cumhurbaşkanı Sarkozy, 20 gün sonra adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakılmıştı.

24 Kasım'da İkizler burcunda gerçekleşen dolunay geride kalırken bazı burçlar için çok daha keyifli bir dönem başlıyor.
Türkiye saatiyle 17.53'te gökyüzünde parlayan bu dolunay, Cafe Astrology 'ye göre iletişim, tutum ve macera duygusuyla ilgili. Uranüs'le aynı hizada olması duygulara sürpriz bir boyut katıyor ve ilişkilerde eski kalıpları kırma isteğini güçlendiriyor. Sitenin yorumuna göre bunun bizim için ne anlama geldiğini önümüzdeki iki haftada keşfedeceğiz.
İşte dolunay sonrası hem aşkta hem de hayatın genelinde yüzü gülecek 5 burç !
Dolunay doğrudan senin burcunda gerçekleşti, yani son günlerde yaşadığın duygusal yoğunluğun bir sebebi vardı. Şimdi o yoğunluk yerini netliğe bırakıyor. Uzun süredir söylemekte zorlandığın şeyleri dile getirmek içini ferahlatacak.
Uranüs'ün de burcunda olması, hiç beklemediğin bir mesajın ya da tanışmanın gündemine girebileceğine işaret ediyor. Bekârsan sıradan bir sohbetin flörte dönüşmesi için çok uygun bir dönemdesin.
Güneş senin burcunda, dolunay ise tam karşında, ilişkiler evinde gerçekleşti. Bu yüzden partnerinle ya da hayatına yeni girecek biriyle ilgili gerçekleri artık çok daha net görüyorsun.
Dolunay sonrası günlerde ufkunu genişletecek bir yolculuk, yeni bir eğitim ya da yepyeni bir çevre karşına çıkabilir. Sevdiğin kişiyle birlikte geleceğe dair plan yapmak için de güzel bir zaman.
Hava grubundan bir dolunay olduğu için onun uyumlu enerjisini en rahat hissedenlerden birisin. Dokuzuncu evini aydınlatan bu dolunay, hayatına yeni bir bakış açısı getiriyor.
Uzak bir yerden gelen bir haber, bir seyahat planı ya da bambaşka bir dünyadan gelen biri kalbini hızlandırabilir. İlişkin varsa birlikte yeni bir şey deneyimlemek bağınızı güçlendirecek.
Dolunay beşinci evinde, yani aşk, eğlence ve yaratıcılık alanında gerçekleşti. Burcunun modern yöneticisi Uranüs'ün dolunayla aynı hizada olması da bu etkiyi sana daha yakın kılıyor.
Önümüzdeki günlerde içindeki çocuğu ortaya çıkaracak, kahkahayla dolu anlar yaşayabilirsin. Kalbini hoplatan biriyle ilk adımı atmak için cesaretin hiç bu kadar yüksek olmamıştı.
Dolunay on birinci evini, yani arkadaşlıklar ve sosyal çevre alanını aydınlattı. Bu da yeni insanlarla tanışmak ve davetlere 'evet' demek için harika bir zaman demek.
Aşk, tam da bir arkadaş grubunun içinden, hiç beklemediğin bir anda çıkabilir. Uzun süredir hayalini kurduğun bir dileğin gerçekleşmesi için de yollar açılıyor.

İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi, Anadolu'nun köklü uygarlıklarından Lidya Krallığı'nın son dönemini konu alan "Edusa" operasını yeniden sahneye taşıyor. Geçtiğimiz sezon dünya prömiyerini yapan eser, kasım ve aralık aylarında Atatürk Kültür Merkezi'nde (AKM) dört temsille izleyici karşısına çıkacak.
Bestesi Güldiyar Tanrıdağlı'ya, librettosu Prof. Dr. İskender Pala'ya ait opera, MÖ 6. yüzyılda Anadolu'nun önemli uygarlıklarından biri olan Lidya Krallığı'nın son döneminde yaşanan siyasi mücadeleleri, Pers tehdidini ve dönemin insan ilişkilerini ele alıyor.
Başkent Sard'ın ekonomik zenginliği ve siyasi gücüyle öne çıkan Lidya Krallığı'nı odağına alan eser, tarihsel olayları adalet, toplumsal düzen ve etik değerler çerçevesinde anlatıyor. Opera, bir uygarlığın kalıcılığının yalnızca toprakları ve maddi zenginliğiyle değil, kuşaktan kuşağa aktardığı kültürel miras ve değerlerle de şekillendiği düşüncesinden hareket ediyor.
Rejisör Caner Akın'ın sahneye koyduğu "Edusa", geleneksel opera anlatımını çağdaş ve deneysel sahneleme teknikleriyle bir araya getiriyor. Dekor, kostüm, ışık ve video tasarımlarıyla Lidya'nın tarihsel dünyasını sahneye taşıyan prodüksiyon, görsel unsurları müzikal anlatımla buluşturuyor.
İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi Orkestrası'nı İbrahim Yazıcı'nın yöneteceği eserin dekor ve görsel tasarımını Efter Tunç, kostüm tasarımını Olcay Engin Kaymaz, ışık tasarımını Cem Yılmazer, video tasarımını Aisha Hajiyeva üstleniyor. Koreografisi Berk Sarıbay'a ait prodüksiyonun korosunu ise Anıl Aydın hazırlıyor.
Edusa karakterini Gülbin Günay ve Evren Işık Yasemin dönüşümlü olarak canlandıracak. Halludas rolünde Mert Süngü ve Ufuk Toker, Krezüs rolünde Göktuğ Alpaşar ve Gökhan Ürben, Namirek rolünde Nesrin Gönüldağ ve Asude Karayavuz, Kyros rolünde Yoel Keşap ve Hüseyin Likos, Solon rolünde Caner Akgün ve Kevork Tavityan, Karuna rolünde ise Barbora Hitay ve Deniz Likos sahne alacak.
Prodüksiyonun geniş kadrosunda ayrıca Berk Dalkılıç, Bülent Külekçi, Alper Göçeri, Murat Güney, Kenan Dağaşan, Emre Güngör, Burak Kul, Talip Savranbaşı, Arda Durgut, Ufuk Karakoç, Efe Doğrukul, Bahadır Özkoca, Uğur Etiler, Okan Fidan, Mehmet Tükel Acar, Fuat Kılıç Aslan ve Mehmet Eminhan Turgut ile İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi'nin bale ve modern dans sanatçıları da yer alıyor.
Geçtiğimiz sezon dünya prömiyerini yapan ve İstanbul Devlet Opera ve Balesi repertuvarına giren "Edusa", 26 ve 28 Kasım ile 10 ve 12 Aralık 2026 tarihlerinde Atatürk Kültür Merkezi Türk Telekom Opera Salonu'nda sahnelenecek.

Ay, 24 Kasım Salı akşamı 17.53'te İkizler burcunda dolunay evresine giriyor ve Ocak'tan bu yana ilk süper ay olarak gökyüzünde daha büyük, daha parlak görünüyor. İletişim, merak ve ikilik temalarını öne çıkaran bu dolunaya Uranüs eşlik ediyor; bu da beklenmedik haberler ve ani fikir değişiklikleri anlamına geliyor. Dolunayın her burçta dokunduğu alana göre bu geceye yakışan 12 film belli oldu.
Ay, 24 Kasım Salı akşamı Dünya'ya en yakın noktalarından birinde dolunay evresine giriyor ve normalden daha büyük, daha parlak görünüyor. Astrolojide İkizler; iletişim, merak, kelimeler ve ikilik demek. Güneş'in Yay'da, Ay'ın karşısında İkizler'de olduğu bu gecede söylenmemiş sözler gün yüzüne çıkıyor.
Uranüs'ün eşlik etmesi ise beklenmedik haberlere ve ani fikir değişikliklerine işaret ediyor. Dolunayın her burçta dokunduğu alana göre seçilen filmler şöyle:
İkizler dolunayı Koç burcunun iletişim, yakın çevre ve kısa yolculuklar alanını aydınlatıyor. Ertelediğin bir konuşma bu günlerde kendiliğinden gündeme gelebilir.
Richard Linklater'ın 1995 yapımı Gün Doğmadan (Before Sunrise), Viyana'da tanışan iki yabancının sabaha kadar süren sohbetini anlatıyor. Ethan Hawke ve Julie Delpy'nin filmi, tek bir konuşmanın bir hayatı nasıl değiştirebileceğini gösteriyor.
Dolunay Boğa'nın para ve kaynaklar alanında. Kazancını, harcamalarını ve kendine biçtiğin değeri yeniden düşünebilirsin.
Bong Joon-ho'nun Oscar'da En İyi Film ödülünü kazanan ilk İngilizce olmayan yapım olarak tarihe geçen Parazit, yoksul bir ailenin zengin bir ailenin hayatına sızışını anlatırken para ile değer arasındaki çizgiyi sorgulatıyor.
Dolunay doğrudan senin burcunda ve Uranüs de hemen yanında. Kimliğin, imajın ve kendini nasıl gördüğün konusunda ani bir aydınlanma yaşayabilirsin.
7 Oscar kazanan Her Şey Her Yerde Aynı Anda, çoklu evrenlerde kendi farklı versiyonlarıyla karşılaşan Evelyn'in hikayesini anlatıyor. Michelle Yeoh'nun başrolündeki film , İkizler'in ikilik temasına bu kadar uyan nadir yapımlardan.
Yengeç için dolunay bilinçaltı ve geride bırakılması gerekenler alanında gerçekleşiyor. Kafanda dönüp duran bir anıyı ya da ilişkiyi kapatma zamanı gelmiş olabilir.
Jim Carrey ve Kate Winslet'in başrolündeki 2004 yapımı Sil Baştan, ayrıldığı sevgilisini hafızasından sildirmeye karar veren bir adamı anlatıyor. Peki unutmak gerçekten iyileştirir mi?
Dolunay Aslan'ın arkadaşlıklar, topluluklar ve gelecek hayalleri alanında. Hayatındaki insanların sana ne kattığını daha net göreceksin.
Gerçek bir hikayeden uyarlanan Can Dostum, felçli zengin bir adamla ona bakıcılık yapmaya başlayan genç Driss arasındaki beklenmedik dostluğu anlatıyor. François Cluzet ve Omar Sy'nin uyumu hâlâ hafızalarda.
Başak burcu için dolunay kariyer ve toplumdaki konum alanında. İş hayatında bir sonuç alabilir ya da yön değiştirmeye karar verebilirsin.
Meryl Streep ve Anne Hathaway'li Şeytan Marka Giyer, hırs ile kendin olmak arasında kalan Andy'nin hikayesi. Üstelik filmin devamı bu yıl 1 Mayıs'ta vizyona girdi; ikisini art arda izlemek için daha iyi bir gece yok.
Dolunay Terazi'nin yolculuklar, eğitim ve yeni bakış açıları alanında. İçindeki kaçma isteği bu günlerde iyice yüksek sesle konuşabilir.
Ben Stiller'ın yönetip başrolünü üstlendiği Walter Mitty'nin Gizli Yaşamı, hayallerinde yaşayan bir arşiv çalışanının İzlanda'ya uzanan gerçek bir maceraya atılmasını anlatıyor.
Akrep burcu için dolunay sırlar, ortak paralar ve derin bağlar alanında gerçekleşiyor. Bir ilişkide perde arkasında kalan bir gerçek ortaya çıkabilir.
David Fincher'ın 2014 yapımı Kayıp Kız, evlilik yıldönümünde ortadan kaybolan Amy ile şüphelerin odağındaki kocası Nick'i anlatıyor. Rosamund Pike'ın performansı Oscar adaylığı getirmişti.
Güneş senin burcunda, dolunay ise tam karşında, yani ilişkiler ve ortaklıklar alanında. Partnerinle ya da yakın bir dostunla ilişkiyi tanımlayan bir konuşma yapabilirsin.
Senaryosu Nora Ephron'a ait Harry Sally ile Tanışınca, 'Kadınla erkek arkadaş olabilir mi?' sorusunu yıllara yayılan sohbetlerle tartışıyor. Billy Crystal ve Meg Ryan'ın filmi tam bir kış klasiği.
Oğlak için dolunay günlük düzen, sağlık ve iş alışkanlıkları alanında. Neyin seni yorduğunu, neyin iyi geldiğini ayırt etmenin tam zamanı.
Wim Wenders'ın Perfect Days (Mükemmel Günler) filmi, Tokyo'da tuvalet temizleyen Hirayama'nın sade ama dolu dolu günlerini izliyor. Kōji Yakusho bu rolle Cannes'da En İyi Erkek Oyuncu ödülünü kazanmıştı.
Dolunay Kova'nın aşk, yaratıcılık ve keyif alanını aydınlatıyor. Bir tutku ya da heyecan verici bir flört gündemine girebilir.
Damien Chazelle'in 6 Oscar kazanan La La Land filmi, Los Angeles'ta hayallerinin peşindeki bir caz piyanisti ile oyuncu adayının aşkını anlatıyor. Ryan Gosling ve Emma Stone'un filmi, hayaller ile aşk arasındaki seçimi sorgulatıyor.
Balık burcu için dolunay ev, aile ve kökler alanında gerçekleşiyor. Ailenle ilgili bir mesele çözülebilir ya da geçmişe dair bir duygu yeniden canlanabilir.
Çağan Irmak'ın 2005 yapımı Babam ve Oğlum, yıllar sonra oğluyla köyüne dönen Sadık ile babası Hüseyin Efendi'nin hikayesini anlatıyor. Çetin Tekindor ve Fikret Kuşkan'ın filmi, izleyenlerin gözyaşlarını tutamadığı yapımların başında geliyor.

Anthropic’in yazılım geliştiricileri için sunduğu kodlama ajanı Claude Code gibi ürünlerin hızla benimsenmesi ve şirketin Ekim ayı sonunda 81 milyar dolarlık gelir oranı, güçlü satış argümanı oluşturdu.
