Rayan Cherki (left) rescued a late draw for Manchester City against Napoli
Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt.
The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.
It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.
Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.
City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.
Maresca said: "We are always looking for three points but when you are not able to win it is important you that don't lose. We take the point, five games [played],10 points and overall I think it is a good result in the end.
"Today, off the ball, once again we didn't concede a lot, the problem is that in this moment they are clinical when we concede a chance, almost every time it is finishing with a goal. We created many chances but in this moment it is like this and move on.
"The first 10 games we always scored first and then in this moment it is exactly in the opposite way, we just need to find a way to avoid that, but I don't think it affects the players in terms of their confidence. We fought until the end."
City were strong favourites for this game and should have had few issues in collecting all three points against a Napoli side that are languishing in eighth place in Serie A.
Their injury issues mean they were able to name only seven substitutes, two of those being goalkeepers, while they had suffered defeat in their past three meetings with City.
They threatened a shock result after twice going ahead through well-taken goals from Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang, but Rayan Cherki managed to salvage a late draw for the hosts.
Maresca's side had 62.7% possession and attempted 665 passes, which largely lacked incisiveness, and of that figure 303 were in the final third compared to Napoli's 77.
The latest disappointing result means City's perfect start is quickly unravelling, now having won only one of their past seven games in all competitions inside 90 minutes.
"It was really surprising to see Manchester City so dull in the first half and so predictable," former Scotland winger Pat Nevin said on BBC Radio 5 Live.
"If you play a team that takes their time, you get yourself set. It is 100% easier to defend.
"You sit and watch City pass, pass, pass, slow, slow. You can get a cigar out."
Star striker Erling Haaland has been in prolific form again this season, scoring 20 goals for club and country, but the 26-year-old has drawn a blank in his past two games.
The Norwegian had chances but failed to score against Fulham on Saturday and though he was handed the captain's armband against Napoli, Haaland was on the periphery for much of the game.
The frontman managed only 14 touches of the ball against the Serie A side on Tuesday, the lowest figure of any player that started the match.
It raises the question whether he is receiving the service to try and find the back of the net.
"I feel I am getting more than enough chances to score," Haaland told TNT Sports. "We tried to push at the end for a goal but we couldn't. Not good enough and we let them in too easy.
"Football is easy and difficult; when you win it's easy and you know what to do, when you don't you start questioning everything. The perfect thing would be to not think but it's not so easy."
City are sixth in the Champions League table, before Wednesday's games, but in the Premier League they have failed to win their past four.
It does not get any easier this weekend, facing a daunting trip to leaders Arsenal on Sunday as they aim to find some form.
Haaland added: "It's the most difficult game of the season going to the champions away.

Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card in loss at Liverpool after call was overturned; Man Utd boss Mauricio Pochettino: "What were VAR doing?"; Poch also believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Mauricio Pochettino has heavily criticised VAR in Manchester United's loss at Liverpool after Leny Yoro's red card was overturned, while the Argentine believes Dominik Szoboszlai’s opener should not have stood.
Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off.
Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool.
It is the second time this season VAR has wrongly gone against Man Utd after ProRef admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford in September.
United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision to award Erling Haaland's winner, which was initially ruled offside before VAR overturned the decision.
Pochettino mentioned the Haaland call in a passionate outburst over VAR as he questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.
Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.
"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?
"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.
"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way.
"We love and accept the technology, but what are they doing? But it's not only this mistake or the mistake for Haaland against Manchester City, it's how after it affects everything."
Pochettino then insisted that Liverpool's opening goal should not have stood because Bradley Barcola was touching the Manchester United wall as Szoboszlai struck in.
Pochettino referenced a similar call last season, which saw Eberechi Eze's free-kick goal for Crystal Palace at Chelsea disallowed after ex-Palace captain Marc Guehi pushed Moises Caicedo to create a gap for the ball to fly through.
The IFAB Laws of the Game state: "If, when a free-kick is taken, an attacking team player is less than 1 m (1 yd) from a 'wall' formed by three or more defending team players, an indirect free-kick is awarded."
Pochettino believes that the law applied to Szoboszlai's free-kick opener due to Barcola's involvement.
He said: "No one talks about that the goal wasn't legal, it should be disallowed because (Bradley) Barcola was touching our wall. Maybe in the last two years, they've maybe changed the rule because I've been in America, but last season when (Eberechi) Eze scored for Palace (at Chelsea) you can see [it was disallowed].
"But VAR didn't check [Dominik Szoboszlai's goal]; that must be disallowed.
"But this type of situation, I need to defend my players and my club, and that is to denounce and to say we were right and the decision wasn't good, and now the three points, where are they?
"I think it's a thing we need to think a little bit more deeper and it's not for tomorrow's game.
"It's about to be tough in the way we use the technology. We need to move on. I'm so proud of the players in the way they manage these unfair situations that happen on the field.
"Our focus now is to improve, to start to win games and tomorrow we have a great opportunity here."
In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at ProRef, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.
Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR, John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.
Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.
"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."

Will Lankshear was back among the goals as Middlesbrough cemented their position at the top of the Championship with a 2-1 win over Swansea City.
Lankshear had missed the final two games prior to the international break because of a hamstring injury, and was only afforded a late substitute appearance in Saturday's win over Bristol City.
Having been restored to the starting line-up at the Riverside, the Championship's leading scorer claimed his 14th league goal of the season to reestablish his side's lead in the second half after Joseph Opoku's driven finish had cancelled out Myles Peart-Harris' opener.
Lankshear's winner came nine minutes into the second half, but the England Under-21 international was also heavily involved in the slick passing move that led to Boro opening the scoring in the ninth minute.
Lankshear's first-time pass released Neto Borges into the left of the area and when he squared across the face of the box, Peart-Harris slotted home a first-time strike of his own to claim his first goal since joining Middlesbrough in the summer.
Boro's lead lasted 13 minutes, with Swansea levelling when Lankshear was at fault at the opposite end of the field.
The striker bundled over Elijah Just on the edge of the area to concede a free-kick. Ben Cabango's goalbound header was nodded off the line by Ashley Phillips, but the ball broke to Opoku, who drilled home an excellent low finish from the edge of the area.

Boro went close to regaining their lead when Riley McGree fired a first-time strike just wide from a corner, and threatened again just before the interval when Peart-Harris volleyed over at the back post after David Strelec flicked Borges' cross into his path.
Swansea remained a threat though, and six minutes into the second half Adilson Malanda played Eom Ji-sung onside as Opoku's through ball unpicked the Boro defence, only for goalkeeper Radek Vitek to burst from his line to keep out the midfielder's shot with his foot.
It was a crucial save as just three minutes later Boro were scoring their second goal at the other end. Callum Brittain's pass sent Peart-Harris breaking away down the right, and when he squared the ball across the face of goal Lankshear was left with the easy task of tapping home.
Sebastian Berhalter should have added a third goal with 18 minutes remaining, but after coming off the bench the American midfielder dragged a shot wide from the right of the area.
His fellow replacement, Max Arfsten, also wasted a good late opportunity, drilling a low strike straight at goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux.
"I'm very happy. It's been a good week, with two wins from two tough games in different ways. We played two good sides, who make it difficult for you, and I'm happy to have come away with six points, six well-deserved points.
"If you look at the Bristol City game, then I think it's difficult to be free-flowing against 10 men in their own box with no intent of putting any pace in the game. I think it's difficult for any teams in the world when it becomes like that. It becomes about winning, and we did.
"This game was a little bit more back and forth. We created a lot of chances and should have scored four or five goals, but overall I'm very happy."
"I'm happy with the players. I'm pleased with the way they've applied themselves in the last two games, that's been second to none. The application has been excellent, listening to what we've been trying to do and then executing it.
"I think we can be better in possession, and if there's a disappointing thing, it's that. I think we're a better team than we're showing in possession.
"Middlesbrough are a good team. They make it difficult for you and put you in awkward positions when they have the ball, then when the ball turns over, I think that's something we could do a little bit better and where we have to get better at.
"I think we made it uncomfortable for Middlesbrough at times, and are probably disappointed not to get something out of the game. But there's lots of things we can learn from and improve on."

Man Utd to contact ProRef and the Premier League over 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card; In the latest Match Officials Mic'd Up , ProRef chief refereeing officer Howard Webb analyses decision as audio of how officials handled incident is revealed
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player
Manchester United will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Leny Yoro's red card against Liverpool.
Yoro was sent off after eight minutes of Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield and was due to face a one-match ban for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity when he brought down Alexander Isak outside the box as he was in on goal.
But Man Utd have had the suspension lifted after a successful claim of wrongful dismissal, the FA said on Tuesday. The independent commission will publish the written reasons in "due course".
Referees' chief Howard Webb backed the process of the officials who sent off the Manchester United defender.
Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol: “I've looked back at past decisions of these commissions to see the make-up of the panel. "In the case of Brentford striker Igor Thiago - who was sent off for elbowing an opponent against Brighton earlier this month - the panel was made up of two former players in Tony Agana and Francis Benali, and a former referee, Steve Bennett.”
However, United boss Mauricio Pochettino questioned why the VAR did not intervene to overturn the on-field decision.
Speaking at a press conference ahead of his team's Champions League match against Sporting in Lisbon on Wednesday, Pochettino said: "Very disappointed because I think this type of thing never can happen.
"My question was always the same - we can accept the referee can make a mistake because of the emotional relationship with the game.
"But if we have VAR, what were they doing? What were they doing? No, because now we are going to repeat the game? We're going to have the possibility to play with the similar tools, 11 against 11?
"The problem is that when we were there, I think they need to take their time to review the situation.
"We have an unbelievable car but we need to be in the level to drive, we need to drive in the best way."
In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at ProRef, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.
Audio from the officials reveals that the VAR, John Brooks, who backed Barrott's decision, determined Isak was "likely" to get on the end of the ball before Lammens. His assistant VAR, Paul Howard, agreed.
Webb was non-committal in his verdict but backed the process of the officials by saying "most people would see that as a correct decision".
"There's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens," said Webb. "Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.
"The VAR checks that to see whether that decision made on the field was clearly and obviously incorrect and formed the opinion that it wasn't. If there was any doubt, then it was doubt.
"It wasn't going to be something that was clearly and obviously wrong and therefore allowed that decisive on-field decision to stand. And I think by and large most people would see that as a correct decision with Isak moving quickly on towards that ball.
"The alternative view is that Lammens might get there first, but I think it's a little bit debatable, I guess. Certainly not clearly wrong."
Manchester United strongly believe the incident was a result of a process error and a failure to interpret the rules correctly.
Club sources believe on the VAR audio there is a quick look and consensus to support the referee with no meaningful challenge or consideration there was an error.
United are also understood to be unhappy there has been no recognition from ProRef that the red card was incorrect after the disciplinary panel overturned the decision.
United believe it is not a subjective decision. If Isak had maintained his top-recorded speed, he still could not have reached the ball before Senne Lammens and the club believe it is objectively provable and they could have shown this on the data within minutes.
ProRef did not want to comment further when contacted by Sky Sports News .
Earlier this season, Pro Ref admitted an error in awarding Manchester City's winner at Manchester United in their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford and contacted the club to explain how the VAR "should have recommended an on-field review" for Erling Haaland's winner.
Sky Sports News understands United received an apology over the incorrect VAR decision.
REF - Sam Barrott: DOGSO (Denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity), DOGSO.
REF: Outside and it's a red card for DOGSO. On-field decision is outside, red card for DOGSO.
VAR - John Brooks: Checking the on-field decision of DOGSO. Longer loop, please.
VAR: Yeah, point of contact. Go 18 [yard] now, go 18. Clearly outside. First contact, clearly outside.
VAR: So, Isak is the right side, defender is the wrong side. Defender bundles into him, into the back. Gets too tight. I think it's a foul. Go back to 18-yard. Let's roll it through, firstly to see whether the attacker is going to get on the end of the ball. Just roll it through, real speed.
VAR: So, at full speed, Isak maintains his momentum and likely gets on the end of it. Certainly not clearly wrong that he doesn't. So I think the DOGSO is confirmed. We'll just check APP (Attacking Possession Phase).
VAR: Sam [referee], the DOGSO location and sanction is confirmed. Just checking the rest of the APP.
VAR: Yeah: Frame two, clearly onside. We've seen it all. Doesn't control the ball with the arm or anything, yes. Sam, confirming the on-field decision of a free-kick to Liverpool just outside the box and a denial of a goalscoring opportunity.
"Firstly, I think this was a really decisive decision by the referee Sam Barrott. We know it is clearly a foul and we also know it is outside the penalty area.
"We're thinking about the sanction. Is it a denial of an obvious goal scoring opportunity? There's actually four considerations officials have to think about.
"Direction of play: he is definitely going towards the goal. It's not going out wide. Proximity from goal: it's just outside the penalty area.
"The location of other defenders: there's only Yoro there. The keeper is moving back towards his own goal. He has to put the brakes on and possibly come back out.
"The reason we're talking about it is the fourth consideration. That's control or likelihood of keeping on or gaining control of the ball. Isak's got control of the ball. He's got possession. He's got the touch. He knocks it past Yoro. He's moving at pace at that moment. And a foul comes in and knocks him down.
"And there's a question mark, I guess, around whether or not he would get onto that ball before Lammens. Now, in the moment, the referee looked at it and felt he would. That was the referee's call made on the field.

Match report as Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli in the Champions League at the Etihad Stadium. Rasmus Hojlund and Noa Lang twice put the Italian side in front but equalisers from Ayyoub Bouaddi and Rayan Cherki earned Enzo Maresca's men a point
Rayan Cherki’s late strike salvaged a 2-2 draw for Manchester City at home to Napoli in the Champions League but Enzo Maresca’s side again struggled to find their fluency.
Former Manchester United striker Rasmus Hojlund opened the scoring for the Italian side and though Ayyoub Bouaddi equalised, Noa Lang's volley stunned the Etihad Stadium as Napoli restored their lead late on. Cherki's goal at least secured a point.
The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet. Maresca's men look vulnerable ahead of the trip to Arsenal on Sunday.
With little to cheer in the first half, the home crowd took most pleasure in serenading Kevin De Bruyne on his return - King Kev declared one banner - and he gave glimpses of his quality, twice cutting City's defence apart. But the sluggish tempo suited a veteran.
It was all a little too slow from City. Maresca was trying to tighten up in midfield, picking Bouaddi as well as Elliot Anderson and Enzo Fernandez for only the second time. But it left this City side short of thrust in the last third despite Allan's impressive endeavour.
It needed a strong save from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City went in level at the break. Sam Beukema made firm contact with a free header inside the box but the Napoli defender placed it too close to the goalkeeper. The home side did not heed the warning.
Billy Gilmour fed Hojlund inside the box on the angle and he got the shot away under pressure from Marc Guehi to beat Donnarumma low to his left. It was a sweet moment for the Danish striker, 23, whose United links had seen him booed by the City fans.
Enzo Maresca satisfied with Manchester City's score-draw vs Napoli in the Champions League

'Brilliant performance' - Mikel Arteta 'pleased' with Arsenal's display vs Borussia Dortmund

But Napoli's lead did not last long thanks to Bouaddi. The elegant Moroccan midfielder had yet to score a goal at senior level in his career but his left-footed effort found its way through Vanja Milinkovic-Savic. Substitute Jeremy Doku provided the spark required.
City were pushing for a winner at that stage, but Lang's exquisite volley on the counter-attack was a reminder that Maresca is having trouble controlling counter-attacks. At least he had kept the mercurial Cherki on the pitch to help avoid a damaging defeat.
But after that seven-game winning run in the Premier League, it is one point from four domestically and now this unconvincing effort in front of their own supporters. City are still a work in progress under Maresca. They will need to improve plenty at Arsenal.
The game ended amid confusion when the referee blew the final whistle with the big screen showing around 20 seconds of the two minutes of added time still to play. City were in possession and moving the ball up the pitch. Donnarumma was among those incensed at the decision as City players surrounded the official who responded by pointing to his watch. The problem is that this watch must have been telling a different time to the one everyone else was seeing.
"We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough. We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want.
"Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games everything is easy and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think but it's difficult in these moments.
"We have so much quality. It's about getting that quality out of every single player. We have to regroup to stay positive and bring the energy on the pitch.
"We go to the champions next. The most difficult game of the season. We need a top, top performance."
